newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end off but resist Dow nosedive.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end off but resist Dow nosedive.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed narrowly lower Friday but put in a good performance compared to the shakeout on Wall Street.
However, traders said the outlook remained uncertain ahead of a long weekend and the U.S. Federal Reserve talks Tuesday.
"Things went strangely well, considering the way New York and Brazil tumbled," said Miguel Daneri at Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.2 percent to 838.71 and closed 1.4 percent lower for the week.
"I think we were favored by the participation of local pension fund players, who kept the tone steady," Daneri said.
"But when the market opens again Tuesday it will face the Federal Reserve talks, so it's still pretty risky out there," he added.
Traders also noted the trend remained fairly selective, with some scattered strong gains Friday helping to offset general market losses.
"Several stocks which fared badly earlier in the week recovered today on short-covering, most notably the car sector which had been battered," one dealer said.
Carmakers Sevel and Ciadea bounced back 8.4 percent and 4.8 percent, respectively.
The broad market closed off 0.4 percent, with losers outpacing winners 29 to 17 and 14 stocks closing flat.
Floor volume picked up to 34.8 million pesos from 29.7 million Thursday, but over-the-counter turnover plummeted to 48.3 million pesos against 107.5 million Thursday.

Other top MerVal gainers were utility Central Puerto and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which rose 3.4 percent and 2.0 percent, respectively. Losers were led by textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, oil company Astra and foods giant Molinos, off 4.2 percent, 2.8 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
